issues: This assumes your Flux deployment supports parsing `#flux:` directives when submitting the script via `flux batch script.sh`; otherwise `-c 1` and `-t 48h` must be passed to `flux batch` on the command line.

Only `-c 1` is requested (cores), but no task count (`-n`) is specified; Flux will use its default (commonly 1 task). If Snakemake needs more parallelism in the parent job, performance may be limited.

The Snakemake `--drmaa` string is Slurm-specific (partition, mem, -o/-e, -J) and will submit to Slurm via slurm-drmaa; this is not a Flux resource issue, but it means the workflow's worker jobs won't be managed by Flux.
